narrative:
The model estimated that you have a 30% chance of becoming a bad credit risk. That does not mean default is certain; it means that, among applicants with a similar profile, about three in ten would be expected to run into serious repayment trouble. For this loan product, that estimated risk was still higher than the bank was prepared to accept, so your application was denied.

The strongest influence on the decision was the short repayment period you requested: 9 months, well below the approved average of about 19 months, and this helped your case by lowering the assessed risk. The second strongest influence was the modest amount requested, 1,670 DM, also well below the approved average of about 3,020 DM, and it too helped your case. The third and most important adverse signal was your checking-account balance in the 0-200 DM range; only 18.4% of approved applicants had this balance range, and it pushed the assessment toward bad credit. The denial reflects the overall balance of your profile, not any single item alone.

Next, ask the bank for a written explanation and check your credit report for errors. Strengthening your checking-account balance, providing recent income proof, adding a guarantor or co-applicant, and asking whether a smaller or different loan structure could be reviewed manually would be sensible steps before reapplying.
